items.title: UK refuses to join Trump's Strait of Hormuz blockade

featured_image.name: UK, France eye warships, mine-hunting drones to break Iran's grip ...

items.description:
The United Kingdom confirmed on Sunday that it will not join President Donald Trump's newly announced naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, directly contradicting Trump's own claims that Britain was among the countries assisting with the operation.

Trump announced the blockade in a post on Truth Social hours after US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad collapsed without a deal. "Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz," he wrote. In a later interview with Fox News, Trump said, "The U.K. and a couple of other countries are sending mine sweepers".[1][2]

That claim was swiftly rebuffed by London. A UK government spokesperson told CBS News that Britain would not be involved in the blockade and was instead "urgently working with France and other partners to put together a wide coalition to protect freedom of navigation". The spokesperson added: "The Strait of Hormuz must not be subject to tolling".[3][2]

items.title: Orban concedes as Magyar's Tisza wins Hungary election

featured_image.name: Hungary election: Early results show Magyar’s Tisza ahead of Orban’s Fidesz

items.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban conceded defeat on Sunday night to opposition leader Peter Magyar, whose Tisza party was on course to win a commanding majority in the country's parliamentary election, ending 16 years of uninterrupted rule by Orban's Fidesz party.

Magyar announced the victory in a social media post, saying that Orban had personally sent his congratulations on the election win, according to Euronews. Reuters reported that Orban conceded after projections showed Tisza winning a two-thirds supermajority in the 199-seat National Assembly.[1][2]

items.title: IRGC claims full control of Strait of Hormuz after Trump orders blockade

featured_image.name: Trump threatens Strait of Hormuz blockade after US-Iran ceasefire talks end without agreement

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared on Sunday that its naval forces have assumed full control over all maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, issuing a sharp warning to Washington just hours after President Trump announced a U.S. naval blockade of the critical waterway.

In a statement posted in Persian on X, accompanied by video footage appearing to show vessels targeted in crosshairs, the IRGC naval command said "all traffic is under the full control of the armed forces" and warned that "the enemy will become trapped in a deadly vortex in the Strait if it makes the wrong move". The declaration came as a direct response to Trump's announcement on Truth Social that the U.S. Navy would "effective immediately" begin blockading all ships attempting to enter or leave the strait.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Chinese crystal breaks record in race to build nuclear clocks

featured_image.name: Scientists develop new ammonium fluorooxoborate crystal - CGTN

items.description:
Scientists in China have created the world's first crystal capable of producing the ultraviolet light needed to power thorium nuclear clocks, a development that could one day enable submarines and deep-space probes to navigate without GPS.

The fluorinated borate compound, developed by a team led by Pan Shilie at the Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry, can push laser light down to a record 145.2 nanometres — short enough to meet a critical requirement for these ultra-precise, compact timekeepers, the South China Morning Post reported. The research was published in the journal Advanced Materials earlier this year.[1][2]

items.title: Hungarians vote in election that could end Orban's 16-year rule
items.description:
Hungarians are voting on Sunday in a parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Viktor Orban's 16-year grip on power, with record-high turnout reported in the early hours and opposition challenger Peter Magyar's Tisza party leading in most opinion polls.[1][2][3]

Polling stations opened at 6 a.m. local time and are set to close at 7 p.m., with roughly 8 million citizens eligible to elect the 199 members of the National Assembly. By 11 a.m., turnout had reached 37.98% — the highest ever recorded at that hour and about 12 percentage points above the same point in the 2022 election, according to Hungary's National Election Office. High turnout is widely seen as favoring the opposition.[4][3][5][1]

items.title: Trump orders naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump announces naval blockade on Iran after peace talks ...

items.description:
President Trump announced on Sunday that the US Navy would immediately begin blockading all ships entering or leaving the Strait of Hormuz, a sharp escalation that came just hours after marathon peace talks with Iran in Islamabad ended without a deal.

"Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social, according to CBS News. He said the Navy would also "seek and interdict every vessel in International Waters that has paid a toll to Iran" and begin destroying mines Iran had laid in the waterway. "Any Iranian who fires at us, or at peaceful vessels, will be BLOWN TO HELL!" he added.[1][2]

items.title: Putin offers to mediate after US-Iran talks collapse in Islamabad

featured_image.name: Russia seeks to serve as mediator between US and Iran

items.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Sunday that Moscow stands ready to mediate between the United States and Iran, hours after marathon negotiations in Islamabad ended without an agreement and raised fears that a fragile ceasefire could unravel.

"Vladimir Putin emphasized his readiness to further facilitate the search for a political and diplomatic settlement to the conflict, and to mediate efforts to achieve a just and lasting peace in the Middle East," the Kremlin said in its readout of the call.[1][2]

items.title: Study finds three distinct types of black hole mergers

featured_image.name: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA detect most massive black hole merger to ...

items.description: A team of astrophysicists has found that merging black holes detected through gravitational waves do not all form the same way. Instead, they fall into three distinct subpopulations, each bearing the fingerprints of a different cosmic origin story. The study, submitted to the preprint server arXiv on March 18, draws on data from the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration's latest gravitational-wave catalog, which now contains over 150 confirmed binary black hole detections.[1][2]
